in_english.name: Elimelech
in_english.long_meaning: Elimelech is a Hebrew name meaning God is King, and it is mentioned in the Old Testament as the father of Naomi, and its significance is God who is the ruler

biblical_reference.note: Elimelech was the husband of Naomi and the father of Mahlon and Chilion

data.cultural_impact: The name Elimelech has a deep cultural significance for the Jewish community, as it was the name of a biblical figure mentioned in the Book of Ruth. Elimelech was an ancestor of Ruth and Boaz, and he emigrated from the Land of Israel to the land of Moab along with his wife Naomi and two sons, Mahlon and Chilion. In the biblical narrative, Elimelech and his family experienced poverty and hardship, but their story eventually led to the birth of the legendary royal line of King David and the Messiah. Thus, the name Elimelech continues to evoke a sense of resilience and perseverance in the face of challenges in the Jewish culture.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Elimelech lies in its affirmation of monotheism and belief in God's sovereignty. The name itself proclaims, "My God is God," emphasizing the idea that there is only one deity who rules over all things. For Jewish people, who hold monotheism at the core of their faith, this name carries a deep spiritual meaning as a constant reminder of their devotion to the One True God. Additionally, the name Elimelech can serve as a source of comfort and strength during difficult times, emphasizing that God is the ultimate source of power and guidance in life.

historical_references.reference: Elimelech is mentioned in the Book of Ruth as the name of Naomi's husband and father of her sons Mahlon and Kilion. They left Bethlehem in the land of Judah to live in Moab during a severe famine in about 1100 BCE.
historical_references.context: Biblical account of Naomi and her family's experiences in Moab and their return to Judah

historical_references.reference: Elimelech is also the name of the father of the prophet Elijah in Jewish tradition. He is said to have lived in the northern kingdom of Israel during the 9th century BCE and was a priest at the temple of Baal in Bethel.
historical_references.context: Legendary ancestor of the prophet Elijah in Jewish tradition

name_in_real_life.story: Michael Elimelech, a minister in New York, United States, shares that their name Elimelech meaning "My God is God" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Elimelech means "my God is light" or "God of light". The name symbolizes a strong connection with the divine, seeking guidance and illumination from God amidst life's challenges.
